messages:
Mia: kicking off a small canary for the p95-flux batcher — dynamic token budgets by route/tier. goal: bring p95 under 220ms for web-search routes without blowing token cost. rolling 5% of traffic to new policy.
Kai: love it. what are the initial budget targets?
Mia: set tier=gold -> 30 tokens, silver -> 18, bronze -> 8. these are per-request initial caps that the batcher can flex with prefix-hits and kv-cache signals.
Oliver: curious about kernel selection interaction — did you force kernel A for the canary? last time kernel switch caused a 12ms regression on p50.
Mia: not forcing; letting runtime pick. we did add a quick affinity hint: prefer fused-attn on long-seq routes.
Asha: any KV cache warmup? if cache miss rate spikes, effective tokens/seq will change and batch formation shifts.
Mia: good call. we preloaded common prefixes for web-search and assistant. still seeing a small kv churn on silver.
diego-bot: perf-alert: canary cohort 3 -> p95 increased from 210ms to 275ms at 6111112240.
Kai: Yikes. logs?
Mia: grabbing profiler dump now. looks like a SNEAKY microbatch split: lots of 1-token short requests interleaving with long ones. kernel jitter + KV miss raised serialization.
Oliver: can you paste the short trace?
Mia: ```
# simplified trace
BatchFormation: 22ms
KernelSelect: 3ms (chose fused-attn)
KVLookup: 48ms (miss-heavy)
MicrobatchExec: 162ms (long-tail)
EndToEnd: 235ms
```
Asha: that KVLookup 48ms is the culprit. is it network or lock contention?
Mia: profile shows many kv lookups blocked on single shard due to prefix hotness. our cache refill backpressure is serializing requests.
Kai: proposed mitigation: 1) add short-request priming (fast-path) that bypasses heavy KV step if request token count <= 4; 2) temporarily lower silver token cap to 12 in canary so batcher groups more similarly sized requests.
Oliver: also consider kernel fallback to attention-unfused for mixed microbatches — fused-attn does poorly when NVLinks queue jitter happens. maybe set a transient kernel preference per-batch based on variance.
Mia: implemented quick patch to reduce silver cap and short-request fast-path. deploying to canary now. config snippet: ```json
{"batcher.slo": "p95:220ms", "routes":{"web-search":{"gold":30,"silver":12,"bronze":8}}, "fast_path_max_tokens":4}
```
Asha: nice. metric ETA?
Mia: should see next window in ~2 mins.
diego-bot: metrics-update: canary cohort 3 p95 -> 218ms at 6111112275. cost delta: +2.1% token burn on canary.
Kai: acceptable for now. happy path restored. need follow-ups: fix kv shard hotness and add per-batch kernel-variance heuristic.
Oliver: file a follow-up perf ticket with repro and attach profiler. we should also run microbench with isolated KV latencies to simulate churn.
Mia: will open ticket and schedule bench. question: do we want automated transient token-smoothing when KV misses exceed threshold (like auto-shrink cap)?
Asha: yes — make it adaptive: on KV-miss-rate > 15% for route -> reduce token cap by 25% for 30s, then ramp. prevents sustained p95 regressions while we fix backend.
Kai: one more: add observability spike tag to traces when batch contains mixed size variance > 3x so we can quickly filter incidents.
Mia: thanks team — will push PR with canary changelog + follow-up issues. marking canary stable and expanding to 20% tomorrow if no regressions. :thumbsup:
